newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Horse Racing-Ireland's O'Brien eyes Cheltenham win.
newsitem.headline: Horse Racing-Ireland's O'Brien eyes Cheltenham win.

text.p: Irish trainer Michael O'Brien will bid to bridge a 16-year gap when his stable star Anabatic competes in the Murphy's Gold Cup at Cheltenham on Saturday.
O'Brien, 53, won the race, then known as the Mackeson Gold Cup, with Bright Highway in 1980.
Bright Highway went on to land the Hennessy Gold Cup three weeks later before an injury he picked up schooling kept him out of the Cheltenham Gold Cup.
"The thing with Bright Highway was a cruel disappointment for us," O'Brien said. "He was already the best horse around at the time and he was only six."
Cruel fate was to strike again when a debilitating fall from a horse in South Carolina in 1974 left O'Brien confined to a wheelchair.
O'Brien had been champion jump jockey in the United States at the time of the accident.
He returned to Ireland in 1976 with his brother Leo and set up a training establishment near the headquarters of Irish flat racing on The Curragh, in County Kildare.
"We built the place from scratch and expanded it to 48 boxes, and in our fourth year Michael was champion trainer in Ireland," Leo said.
Michael O'Brien has since landed two Irish nationals and a Triumph Hurdle as well as those titles he landed with Bright Highway.
BETTING: 5-1 Big Matt and Challenger du Luc, 6-1 Dublin Flyer, 7-1 Addington Boy and Anabatic, 8-Kibreet, 10-1 Call It A Day and Absalom's Lady.
